statement: Tom writes the digits of 2026 again and again: 202620262026... What is the sum of the first 30 digits he writes?

choices.misconception: I found 7 full blocks of 2026 in 30 digits, worth 70, and forgot the 2 digits left over.
I divided 30 by 4 to get 7 and a half blocks and took 7 and a half times 10.
I took the 2 leftover digits from the end of a block, 2 and 6, instead of the start.
I rounded up to 8 full blocks of 2026, which is 32 digits, not 30.

hints: How many digits are in one block?
Each block of 4 digits adds the same amount. Find how many whole blocks fit into 30 digits and which digits are left over.
One block, 2 0 2 6, adds up to 10. Thirty digits are 7 blocks with 2 digits left.

solutions.reliable: One block 2, 0, 2, 6 has sum 10. $30 = 7 \times 4 + 2$, so there are 7 full blocks (sum 70) and then the first 2 digits of a new block, 2 and 0. Total: $70 + 2 + 0 = 72$. The transferable idea: in a repeating pattern, count whole cycles, then deal with the leftover from the start of the cycle.

whyOnTest: Repeating cycles: divide by the cycle length and handle the remainder from the start of the cycle.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
